_about: How a restaurant day runs. One day per real day, starting at 5 AM local (GameClock.DAY_STARTS_AT_HOUR). Every day opens at the first phase, whatever the time. Each phase has a set list of customers, planned once a day: walk_ins townsfolk plus some of the day's regulars (regulars_per_day in regulars.json, spread across the phases). When everyone in a phase is done, a player rings the bell at the counter for the next one; after the last, the restaurant closes (big moment scenes play then), the night shift runs if the phone is up, the summary shows, and then it is After Hours until a player opens up on the next restaurant day (see DayCycle). arrival_seconds: the usual gap between customers walking in (shaped by pacing). lighting: the sun's color and energy, the ambient light, and the sky color, faded in as the phase starts. 'closing' is the lighting after the last phase. Once the phone is on the wall, the night shift follows closing: chairs up, no walk-ins, phone orders only (see data/phone.json 'night'); 'night' is its name and lighting.

after_hours._about: After the summary: closed to customers, chairs up, the doors open. The lighting follows the real local hour block (data/time.json), checked every minute.

_pacing: How a meal's customers spread out, as multiples of arrival_seconds: calm_start after the first one, then rush between the rest (called out with rush_text once, in a meal of rush_from or more), and wind_down before the last one in a meal of wind_down_from or more. While there's no free seat they wait outside, trying again every retry_seconds.
